newsitem.title: USA: Voters choose new mayor in Dade County, Fla..
newsitem.headline: Voters choose new mayor in Dade County, Fla..

text.p: Former Dade County Commission Chairman Arthur Teele and County Commissioner Alex Penelas vied in Tuesday's runoff election to become the county's first mayor since voters adopted the strong mayor form of government.

County Elections Supervisor David Leahy predicted voter turnout of 29 percent, more than double the turnout for the last local run-off election in a presidential year, due to the hotly contested mayor election.
"There's not much left on the ballot except for the mayor's race," Leahy said.
Polls showed Penelas leading by as much as 12 points, but analysts said a strong turnout among black voters could help Teele, who is black.

The campaign has turned nasty, with Teele and Penelas each accusing the other of pandering to special interests who have contributed to their campaigns. Neither filed campaign finance reports on time.
Voters approved a strong mayor form of government last November, a move that will give the mayor new powers and major influence over Dade's $4 billion budget.
The county had a mayor until the court ordered a county government reorganization in the early 1990s, but the post was mostly ceremonial.

Also on the Dade ballot is a runoff race between former County Commissioner Barbara Carey and Billy Hardemon, who was chief of staff for County Commissioner James Burke before entering the commission race. The two are vying for the seat commission seat Teele gave up when he decided to run for mayor.
The Miami Herald has reported that federal prosecutors are targeting Hardemon and Burke in a probe of alleged kickbacks involving Dade County bond deals.

Burke and Hardemon denied wrongdoing and neither has been charged. Hardemon initially said he would drop out of the race. But on Sept 23, he said he had declined an FBI offer to cooperate in gathering information against Burke, and that he would continue his campaign in order to fight unjust allegations.
